Summary: Predestination is God's eternal purpose to save His people in Christ, worked out in calling, justification, sanctification, and glorification. In its broadest sense it affirms that salvation rests on God's gracious plan from beginning to end.
HistoricalDevelopment: Developed by Augustine in debates over grace, predestination was taught by Aquinas, emphasized by Luther and Calvin, and debated at the Synod of Dort (1618-1619) and in Arminian responses.
Interpretations: Reformed Christians teach unconditional predestination to salvation, Arminians teach predestination based on God's foreknowledge of faith, and Lutherans and others frame it in distinct ways, while all orthodox views reject salvation by merit.
RelatedTopics: Election; Salvation; Grace; Providence; Free Will
